statusToRegion.why: Scheduling is a delayed publish. Publish-side HERE so it cannot route around the boundary; still an overlay for the reseat, which is a separate decision (Sequence::OVERLAY_STATUSES).
Handed back verbatim. NOT a region — callers filter it before comparing, or trashing a live post reads as an out-of-publish crossing.
Handed back verbatim. Core-internal (revisions, attachments); filtered like trash.

crossesPublishBoundary.why: Two non-publish regions: a reseat, but not a boundary crossing.
`private` is its own region and is not publish-side.
Out of publish. The veto is SYMMETRIC: a user barred from publishing must not be able to unpublish.
Into publish from any non-publish region.
Scheduling is a publish crossing — otherwise cron publishes on the user's behalf and the guard is bypassed.
Re-scheduling a post already in the publish region stays publish-side.
Trash is an overlay that suspends the workflow in place, in either direction.
Core-internal, never a user-initiated editorial move. This is the case that drifted: PHP filtered it, JS did not, so the client vetoed what the server allowed.
